output.sql: SELECT c.country, ROUND(SUM(o.net_revenue), 2) AS revenue FROM marts.fct_orders o JOIN marts.dim_customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.is_revenue AND lower(trim(c.segment)) = 'enterprise' AND o.order_date >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND o.order_date < DATE '2026-01-01' GROUP BY c.country ORDER BY revenue DESC;
output.explanation: Revenue is taken from fct_orders where is_revenue is true, summing net_revenue. Orders are joined to dim_customers to filter on segment 'enterprise' (case and whitespace normalized) and grouped by customer country. The date filter covers order_date in calendar 2025, and results are sorted highest revenue first. I did not run the query, so the segment spelling is assumed to be 'enterprise'.
